checks.title: Entry-timing difference is declared
checks.detail: kernel enters at the hourly close; the live bot scans every 5 min on a forming candle, so the kernel reads pumps +0.59pp larger on average (200 matched setups). DECLARED LIMITATION: arena absolute WR is not live WR. Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel — but a promoted arm must still survive the earlier live entry, and that caveat is attached to every surfaced verdict.

findings.claim: entry_granularity_declared: 'Arm-vs-arm comparisons stay valid — all arms share this kernel' (kernel reads pumps +0.59pp larger than the live bot, 200 matched setups).
findings.problem: A shared bias is only neutral for arms whose parameter is orthogonal to it. entry-8pct is defined by a pump-size threshold (pump_pct=8.0), so a kernel that systematically reads pumps 0.59pp larger admits marginal 7.4-8.0% events into that arm which the live bot would never detect. The bias is differential, not common-mode, and it lands on the arm with the smallest sample (screen_n=496, live_n=3) and the only negative screen_ev (-0.055). The declared limitation covers absolute WR but explicitly waives the comparison, which is exactly where it is not waivable.

findings.claim: STATISTICAL REALITY: 'measured ghost arrival = 25.2 control trades/day' with 'confirm planned n = 600'.
findings.problem: This rate is quoted with no n and no tier label, and it can only come from the backfill tier: events by tier are 4764 backfill vs 50 live, and control's screen_n=1550 over the 62.0-day span is ~25/day, matching it. Live control has taken 13 trades. Using a backfill-derived arrival rate to size the confirm horizon implies n=600 is ~24 days away when the live tape has produced 50 events in total across all arms. A separate graveyard entry (L-dedup-0h) cites the same baseline as 25.6 control trades/day, so the figure is not even internally consistent.

findings.claim: graveyard_enforced ok=true: 'Dead ideas are refused automatically — 47 refutations loaded; probe naming peak-close was refused by G-01'.
findings.problem: The evidence is one positive-control probe on one literal blocked string. The arena itself contradicts the general claim: minprice-1 was registered as an arm and only later killed on narrative grounds as 'G-13 re-executed as a parameter', and dedup-24h and dedup-2h were likewise killed by a written 'history:' review rather than auto-refused, while only dedup-0h and dedup-48h hit an automatic REFUTED_BEFORE match on G-06. Three of six retired arms consumed registration slots that the automatic layer failed to refuse, so the checkbox is green for a reason that does not establish the property it names.

findings.claim: Arena reports screen_dWR=0.0pp for entry-8pct and vol-4x, alongside paired_population ok=true: 'every arm scored on identical events (4814 events)'.
findings.problem: entry-8pct shows screen_wr=51.613 against control's 49.935 and vol-4x shows 51.27, yet both report a delta of exactly 0.0pp — the field is not being computed for filter arms, it is defaulting. Worse, those arms are not scored on identical events at all: screen_n is 496 and 866 versus control's 1550, because their filters decline events. Seeing the shared detection stream is not the same as producing a paired trade on it, and the methodology requires delta vs champion on the SAME window. As displayed, two arms carry an authoritative-looking 0.0pp that is neither their true delta nor a paired one.

findings.claim: backfill_cannot_promote ok=true, critical=true: 'Only live-tape evidence can promote — 0 surfaced arm(s); none promoted from a screen'.
findings.problem: The gate has never been exercised. With zero arms ever surfaced, a rule that promotes on backfill and a rule that refuses to would both produce this identical green. The check confirms an empty set, not a working guard, and it is marked critical — which reads as a verified safety property to anyone scanning the board. Given the arena's largest evidence by two orders of magnitude is backfill (4764 events, screen_n up to 1550) against live_n of 3-13, this is precisely the gate that most needs a real test.

findings.claim: no_lookahead ok=true, critical=true: 'Detection is look-ahead free — re-detected 108 events on truncated history across 6 coins; mismatches: none'.
findings.problem: The probe covers 6 of 176 coins and 108 of 4814 shared-window events, roughly 2%, and the conclusion is stated for the whole system without that coverage caveat attached. It also only re-runs detection; it does not test the exit path, where sl_anchor=peak is the parameter that G-01 and G-21 both died on for peak-related look-ahead and post-hoc clipping. A clean detector spot-check on 2% of the universe does not establish that the scored outcome of every arm is look-ahead free.
